lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about history.
Sam, you went to a museum on Sunday. Tell us!
Yes! It is in the old city. It is very, very old.
I know it. I grew up near it. Was there a king?
Yes! There was a big castle and an old king. I saw his book, his chair and his hat.
What year was it?
I asked the guide. He said, "A long time ago."
[laugh] And the war? Was there a war, a big fight?
I asked, "What happened?" The guide looked at me.
What did he say?
He said, "I don't know."
[laugh] An honest guide! He tells the truth.
Yes. I want to go back next week. Maybe he knows more then.
Or maybe he comes back with a new hat. Bye for now!

words.en: a building with old or interesting things to see
a man who rules a country
something you wear on your head
a way to start a story about the past

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is history. And last night I went to a quiz.
A history quiz! How was it?
Painful. The first question was, "Which century was the Maiden Tower built in?" I said, "Last century."
Sam! It's ancient.
I know that now. A long time ago, I was good at school. Maybe. The next question was about a famous king. I said, "Is he the king from the chess game?"
[laugh] And the third question?
"What important event took place in this city in 1991?" I didn't know. So I called a friend.
Which friend?
You. You didn't answer. You were asleep.
I was asleep, yes. So you lost.
Zero points. My team was called "The Past", and we found out we had no past.
[laugh] Who won?
A team of grandmothers. They set up their table next to the answer sheet.
Next to the answers?
One of them looks very much like your grandmother.
What year was it? 2026. It happened in a restaurant, and I have no comment. Did you discover anything?
Yes. I discovered that I'm better at the present than the past. See you next time!

words.en: put something in place, ready to use
a way to start a story about the past
saying when or where something happened

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is history, and a very confusing Sunday.
Last weekend I took Sam to see some ruins near Baku. Sam, tell the listeners.
It was a big old stone monument. It dates back to the era of an ancient empire, I think. And there was no sign. Not one.
So we asked a guide. He pointed out that it was built after a revolution.
Then another guide said it was from before the empire. And they started to argue.
Right in front of us. Then a school group arrived, and the teacher said, "Children, this is where our ancestors lived."
And one boy asked, "Which ancestors?" Nobody knew.
That's history. Wars break out, empires fall, whole cities are wiped out, and later nobody agrees what happened. Independence came much later, and nobody argues about that. We just get a day off.
My dad says, "History repeats itself." Every time a war breaks out — or his football team loses — he says it. I think he just likes the sentence.
What does he do for fun, apart from quoting?
Salsa. Last week I found his old trophy in a box. A real blast from the past. He danced in the kitchen for an hour.
Did he make history?
He made the whole street laugh. That's history too.
Cultural heritage can be funny. A question for our listeners: which moment in history would you like to see with your own eyes?
And please, check for a sign before you visit. See you next time!

words.en: many countries ruled by one ruler
a day or year; come from a time in the past
a person who shows a place to visitors
tell someone a fact they should notice
do something important that people will remember
